sourceChecks.title: Comparison of 162 mg and 81 mg Aspirin for Prevention of Preeclampsia: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: Among people at increased risk for preeclampsia
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A trial of 400 randomized high-risk participants found similar severe/preterm preeclampsia rates with 162 mg and 81 mg daily aspirin (14.1% vs 17.1%; P=.4).
sourceChecks.limitations: Trial does not establish a cure or prevention across hypertensive disorders; confidence interval included no difference.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: preeclampsia prevention aspirin randomized trial clinical trial recurrence biomarker primary paper maternal fetal outcome

sourceChecks.title: Cerclage in singleton pregnancies with no prior spontaneous preterm birth and short cervix: a randomized controlled trial
sourceChecks.excerpt: There was no significant difference in the primary outcome
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In 90 analyzed participants, preterm birth <35 weeks occurred in 16.3% versus 23.4%; the difference was not significant. Latency and gestational age at delivery were higher in the cerclage group.
sourceChecks.limitations: Selected risk group, small sample; not a universal mechanism or >90% prevention.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: spontaneous preterm birth prevention progesterone cerclage randomized trial primary paper all etiologies prediction efficacy

sourceChecks.title: Nonhormonal therapy for endometriosis: a randomized, placebo-controlled, pilot study of cabergoline versus norethindrone acetate
sourceChecks.excerpt: We observed a decrease in pain scores
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Nine-woman randomized pilot reported decreased pain scores and no serious adverse events with cabergoline.
sourceChecks.limitations: Very small pilot; symptom relief does not demonstrate lesion eradication, infertility reversal, recurrence prevention, immediate reversibility, or zero side effects.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: nonhormonal endometriosis targeted therapy randomized clinical trial pain recurrence fertility primary study

sourceChecks.title: Impact of human ovarian tissue manipulation on follicles: evidence of a potential first wave of follicle activation during fertility preservation procedures
sourceChecks.excerpt: Fresh ovarian tissue was retrieved from 9 women
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Ex-vivo tissue from nine women showed processing-associated changes in PI3K/Hippo follicle-activation markers.
sourceChecks.limitations: Ex-vivo tissue marker study; does not restore ovarian endocrine function, reverse menopause, extend reproductive life, or establish safety/cancer risk.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: human ovarian tissue primordial follicle activation restoration clinical study primary

sourceChecks.title: Layered precision suturing vs. traditional double-layer closure at cesarean: a randomized trial of uterine scar healing and maternal outcomes
sourceChecks.paraphrase: In the 500-person randomized trial, ultrasound-defined poor healing at six months was 7.5% with layered-precision suturing and 15.0% with double-layer closure.
sourceChecks.limitations: Ultrasound surrogate and six-month follow-up; no scarless healing, full biomechanical restoration, future rupture reduction, or accreta outcomes established.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: uterine scar healing cesarean delivery scar tissue uterine regeneration primary clinical study

sourceChecks.title: Fetal programming of polycystic ovary syndrome: Effects of androgen exposure on prenatal ovarian development
sourceChecks.excerpt: Our data indicates that one path
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Prenatal DHT exposure in a mouse model altered ovarian gene expression and mitochondrial measures relevant to PCOS-like developmental programming.
sourceChecks.limitations: Animal model and induced phenotype do not establish the human root cause or a curative treatment.
sourceChecks.searchQuery: root cause polycystic ovary syndrome heterogeneous reproductive metabolic syndrome primary study

sourceChecks.title: Safety and pharmacokinetics of the non-hormonal male contraceptive YCT-529
